original_question: Let M_{d,r}(C) be the moduli space of rank r polystable vector bundles with fixed determinant of degree d on a smooth projective curve C of genus g, in the case gcd(r, d) = 1 so that M_{d,r}(C) is a smooth Fano variety. Is M_{d,r}(C) K-stable for every such curve C, and can one give a modular interpretation of the limiting points of the K-moduli space X_g that contains [M_{d,r}(C)] and is birational to M_g?
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the same Fano varieties considered in the paper, namely M_{d,r}(C), keeps the coprime hypothesis gcd(r,d)=1 used in the paper to ensure smoothness and the Fano property, asks the universal K-stability question for curves C of genus g, and includes the second paper-specific issue of interpreting the limiting points in the relevant K-moduli space birational to M_g.
missing_details: The paper phrases this as a two-part open problem in Section 2.1.2, Problem 9, not as a general conjecture or theorem.
The genus g is fixed and C varies through smooth projective curves of genus g; part (2) concerns the whole locus of points [M_{d,r}(C)] as [C] varies in M_g, not just one fixed variety.
The ambient K-moduli space is determined by the fixed numerical invariants of M_{d,r}(C), so a symbol depending only on g is under-specified unless its dependence on r and d is declared.
The exact nearby context immediately before Problem 9 supplies the hypothesis that M_{d,r}(C) is a Fano variety and is smooth when gcd(r,d)=1; this should remain attached to the definition.
The paper does not say only that the K-moduli space is birational to M_g; it also adds that this birational map is conjecturally isomorphic over M_g if part (1) is true.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should clarify that limiting points means boundary points of that K-moduli compactification containing the locus [M_{d,r}(C)].
The base field is left implicit in Problem 9, so a fully stand-alone version should specify the ambient algebraic-geometric setting explicitly.
refined_question: Fix integers g, r, d with gcd(r,d)=1, and let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g. Let M_{d,r}(C) denote the moduli space of rank-r polystable vector bundles on C with fixed determinant of degree d; as recalled in the paper, M_{d,r}(C) is then a smooth Fano variety. Is M_{d,r}(C) K-stable for every such curve C? Moreover, as [C] varies in M_g, the points [M_{d,r}(C)] lie in a K-moduli space that admits a birational map to M_g and is conjecturally isomorphic over M_g if the first question has an affirmative answer. Can one give a modular interpretation of the limiting points of this K-moduli space?
equivalent_formulation: By Section 2, Theorem 2(2), the first part is equivalent to asking whether delta(M_{d,r}(C)) > 1 for every smooth projective curve C of genus g with gcd(r,d)=1.
justification: The draft is very close to the paper's exact target: it is essentially Problem 9 in Section 2.1.2. I sharpened it by making the problem explicitly two-part, fixing g, r, and d, keeping the smooth-Fano hypothesis exactly as stated in the sentence immediately preceding Problem 9, and clarifying that the second part concerns the K-moduli space containing the locus of the Fano varieties M_{d,r}(C) as C varies in M_g, not just an abstract space X_g with unspecified dependence on r and d. I also retained the paper's conditional phrasing that this birational map is conjecturally an isomorphism over M_g if part (1) holds. The alternate delta-formulation is justified by Theorem 2(2), and the existence of the ambient K-moduli space is supplied earlier by Theorem 4. The nearby context also records the only cited partial result: when g=2 and r=2, K-stability is known for a curve corresponding to a general point in M_g.
